scenario: [LTIM.2.5.1] edge-once — a now()-gated rule fires exactly ONCE on the false->true edge and MUST NOT re-fire on subsequent clock ticks while the condition stays true. This is the guard that distinguishes the correct persistent fact_id-keyed one-shot from the naive `$ClockTick` re-driver (which fires every tick post-maturity, since per-generation refraction resets each pump). Pin: after the clock crosses the 5_s threshold, pump three more times as the clock keeps advancing — the rule still fires only once (rule_fire_order is an exact match).
rules_ds:
import calendar

schema Sensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule after_5_s:
    Sensor where now() > calendar.time(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 5)
->
    log info "time passed"
